framedMotifDiagnosis.finding: Initial segmentation lines recover the known tip closely, but colour-gradient refinement moves it inward by roughly 10 pixels. This happens with the background-covariance gradient metric in all four fully observed failures.
framedMotifDiagnosis.nextExperiment: Require candidate colour-edge refinements to retain an observed foreground/background transition; compare with shadows, blur, clipped and known-layout controls before adoption.

edgeStudy.status: Completed; both unconditional hypotheses rejected as general replacements
edgeStudy.scope: Two fixed foreground-transition constraints for photographic lower-edge refinement. Evaluate only geometry; known corners score results after selection, never drive fitting. All 83 previous inputs plus six shadow/blur/exposure controls. No template fitting is performed in this study.
edgeStudy.baubleRegression: Both alternatives lose the supported in-photo RGB fallback and return the old unsupported proposal with its tip below the photograph.
edgeStudy.visualInspection: Inspected known/estimated corner overlays for the tinted, lighter-background and dim framed controls. The hard crossing rule deforms the lighter-background right corner; the soft rule substantially improves that case but worsens the dim control.
edgeStudy.next: A fixed follow-up applies the positive paper-transition weight only when the existing learned background covariance also supplies the colour-edge metric. It is running on the same 89 inputs. No production detector change has been made; no template reconstruction has been run for these proposals.

earlierCandidateOnBrowserTarget.scope: Feasibility check only: independently re-render the earlier valid five-cut candidate against the browser target. This candidate is NOT supplied to fresh fitting.

fitterSensitivity.interpretation: An earlier valid five-cut candidate remains feature-complete on the browser target. The fresh browser fit chooses four cuts and loses the same small source region. This is evidence of a search robustness problem, not proof of an impossible target. Mask perturbation, settings and runtime scheduling require controlled separation.

comparison.interpretation: At both fixed setting sets, the earlier mask passes with five cuts and the 15-pixel variant fails with four cuts. Fresh Node application-settings results agree with the browser failure. Runtime-only and settings-only explanations do not account for this pattern; finite-time optimization still contributes to numerical variation.

fitterSensitivity.nextProbe: Try cleanup on the lowest-error geometry/paper-valid, feature-complete candidate within the existing polish eligibility band (maxImageError + 0.01). The failing run already found such a six-cut candidate at 3.17% error. Keep the original fallback unless every unchanged check passes.

timingDiagnosis.finding: Both masks begin with 3+3, 4+4 and 5+5 finalists, but the browser-mask run fails to retain the small feature in either 5+5 fit. It expands to 21 extra-grid comparisons versus three, spending 80.997 seconds versus 19.399 in curve refinement. These are saved controlled runs before the cleanup fix, not an isolated repeated speed benchmark.
timingDiagnosis.nextExperiment: Test bounded polishing when a feature-complete near-threshold candidate first becomes available, preserving ordinary candidates, existing acceptance gates and the request deadline. Separately trace the first divergence of the 5+5 phase-positive refinement; current candidate summaries omit phase and cannot locate it precisely.

offlineAdapterCorrection.scope: Full inverse run: 1081 passes and one offline projective-body adapter failure. After an offline-only shared-seam fix, all four projective-body tests and all three foreground adapter tests pass. The first adapter command had a nonexistent foreground test path, which Node ignored; the three tests were therefore run explicitly in the recorded follow-up. All application/runtime files are unchanged. Check, lint, 874 application tests and build were rerun. The entire inverse suite was not rerun after this offline fix.

editableFeatureAudit.scope: Feature retention checked from the actually downloaded editable SVG, parsed and rasterized independently of the fitting engine. This supplements the browser workflow geometry/paper/error checks.

limitations: Bauble still takes about 110 seconds and has irregular border details.
Measured agreement is with the classified photograph, not original cutting-path ground truth.

earlyPolishExperiment.scope: Same photo and settings; two automatic crops differ by 15 classified pixels. One fresh process per policy/crop. Five-cut progress coordinates captured in both policies and feature-audited after the timed solve. No saved templates or ground-truth cuts enter fitting.
earlyPolishExperiment.interpretation: No published five-cut checkpoint on the perturbed mask passes feature fidelity. Negative phase erases the 5 mm² region; positive phase retains 83.75% but loses enclosure. The nearby mask preserves enclosure in positive phase. Control parameters already differ by up to 1.803 mm after grid/clearance preparation, before free refinement, and diverge later. These are parameter differences, not visible-boundary displacement. This is search sensitivity rather than final ranking discarding a passing five-cut checkpoint; coarse initialization, fine-grid fitting and clearance have not yet been separated.
earlyPolishExperiment.policy: One bounded full-resolution polish of the first geometry/paper/feature-valid near-threshold candidate, before additional grids. Preserve candidates, acceptance gates and request deadline.
earlyPolishExperiment.next: Compare the two prepared physical-edge refinement hypotheses on 89 fixed inputs; continue investigating five-cut initialization sensitivity.
